key_insight: This paper introduces autoregressive Boltzmann Generators, aiming to make equilibrium molecular sampling more expressive and efficient than flow-based Boltzmann Generators. The key idea is to relax the limitations of strictly invertible normalizing flows while still enabling exact likelihoods and importance-sampling-based correction.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of efficiently generating uncorrelated equilibrium samples from molecular systems, a core challenge in statistical physics and molecular simulation. Existing Boltzmann Generators often rely on normalizing flows that can be too restrictive in expressivity because of invertibility constraints.
method: Use an autoregressive generative modeling approach for Boltzmann Generator design.
Combine fast sample generation with exact likelihood computation for training and evaluation.
Apply an importance sampling correction to account for model mismatch and recover accurate equilibrium sampling.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work points to a more flexible generative modeling route for scientific sampling tasks where exactness matters. It broadens the design space beyond invertible flows, potentially improving sample quality and efficiency in molecular generation and other physics-informed applications.
